statements.claim_class: A counted-memory consequence of finite reset sufficiency: simultaneous pointwise dominance with the exact existing command-row list and pure initializer. Classical Bellman optimality is credited, not claimed as newly discovered.
classical_ingredients: Markov sufficiency of an observed reset state
Prior nonlinear programming formulations of optimal fixed-size stochastic controllers
statements.conclusion: One controller with exactly the same list of command rows and the same initial label, whose post-report update is a deterministic function of the reset report alone, weakly improves expected cost at every initial density matrix. The finite row-choice Bellman system has a unique nonnegative finite solution x with x_i<=C; the new controller has initial cost operator H(p^1,x).
hypotheses: Finite reported reset instrument as in thm:reset-control: finite Hilbert dimension, commands and reset states, positive semidefinite failure effects, strictly positive conditional mean cost floor, mandatory immediate success stopping, and no closed failure set.
An autonomous controller with at most M live labels, fixed command rows p^1,...,p^M, prescribed pure initial label 1, and finite cost bounded by C for every initial density matrix.

The observation port includes only the declared report and the controller knows its own sampled command; it has no free state measurement, cost observation, clock, hidden initial label mixture or additional history store.
statements.identity: R78 numbered author addition; the inventory includes lemmas and corollaries and is not a novelty or editorial verdict.
internal_load_bearing_facts: The original all-initial-state guarantee includes starting from every reset density sigma_i with label 1. This supplies a finite comparison policy from every reset state using the same row list; a single-prior guarantee would not suffice.
Value iteration for the finite row choices is bounded by C, and any Bellman-minimizing deterministic selector is proper by the positive mean cost floor.
The actual replacement writes one of the existing labels after each reset report. The comparison restart in the proof is not granted as a physical or memory operation.
statements.label: thm:r78-palette-normal-form
statements.limits: No assertion that all command rows can be made pure, no general partially observed-process normal form, no properness inference from a single initial preparation, and no convexification of the memory constraint.
statements.proof: Treat existing fixed command distributions as finite choices on the observed reset states. Restarting the original controller at label 1 from each sigma_i bounds finite-horizon optimal row-choice values by C. Monotone value iteration gives a finite Bellman solution. Greedy equality and the positive conditional mean cost floor prove finite expected duration, vanishing bounded potential, and exact costs. Bellman inequalities dominate every history policy using these rows, including those remembering sampled commands and private coins; after each first failure the reset state alone fixes the continuation lower. The deterministic selector attains all these continuation lowers using existing labels, proving simultaneous initial-state dominance and uniqueness.

statements.claim_class: An exact entire hard-memory cost frontier, compact budget certificate, and synthesis theorem for the stated reset class, extending the inherited optimum-threshold and first-residual lower certificate. The semialgebraic methods themselves are classical.
classical_ingredients: Bellman supersolutions and stochastic shortest-path verification
Positive semidefinite matrix order and the spectral variational principle
Prior nonlinear programming formulations of optimal fixed-size stochastic controllers
statements.conclusion: The complete constrained value V_M is the attained finite minimum of lambda_max H(p^1,x) over M command rows, one deterministic selector of rows for each reset report, and x in [0,C0]^s satisfying the displayed Bellman supersolution inequalities. For budgets b in [0,C0], adding H<=bI is necessary and sufficient for an actual M-label controller. This determines the exact optimal-memory threshold without strict positive exposure, and gives a strict gap at every insufficient M. Algebraic primitive data yield finite exact algebraic synthesis, without polynomial-time or fixed-M minimax claims.
hypotheses: The full finite reset class and observation conventions of thm:reset-control, with positive mean cost floor and no closed failure set; failure effects may be merely positive semidefinite.
M>=1 counts live controller labels and includes the prescribed pure initial label.
A fixed full-support command distribution supplies the explicit finite one-label cap C0 from eq:r78-explicit-cap.
statements.identity: R78 numbered author addition; the inventory includes lemmas and corollaries and is not a novelty or editorial verdict.
internal_load_bearing_facts: The full-support one-label controller is proper from all reset states, and its reset costs are no larger than its own worst-initial-state spectral cost C0.
Every finite supersolution produces a proper selector and a physical cost operator no larger than H because all failure effects are positive semidefinite.
Every competing controller with robust value <=C0 has a row-choice Bellman vector <=C0, including at reset states unexposed by a particular dual preparation.
The feasible union has finitely many selectors and compact row/vector variables, giving attained rather than merely infimal cost.
statements.label: thm:r78-reset-frontier
statements.limits: The result is not a closed form for arbitrary inputs or a polynomial algorithm; it does not solve the original squared-sign risk frontier, general partially observed control, or arbitrary stopping. The precise row-initializer convention and all-initial-state quantifier are retained.
statements.proof: Prove both budget implications. A supersolution bounds finite-prefix continuation cost; the positive floor gives properness, and positivity of the initial failure effects gives H as an upper cost certificate. Conversely apply the same-row normal form to any controller with robust cost b<=C0; its Bellman vector lies in the compact cube and supplies equality constraints plus H<=bI. The one-label baseline makes the finite union nonempty, compactness yields an optimum, and equality of feasible budgets identifies it with the original controller infimum. Finite unrestricted implementation bounds the saturation memory. With algebraic data, simplex, supersolution and Hermitian principal-minor constraints are real-algebraic; elimination and sample-point selection give exact values and attaining coordinates.

statements.claim_class: Stability of the exact counted-memory reset frontier derived from the compact certificate and transient optimal realization.
classical_ingredients: Continuity of finite matrix resolvents and eigenvalues
statements.conclusion: V_M is continuous in the primitive effects, mean costs and reset states throughout the valid class. Every strict gap V_M>V_* persists locally. This is a statement about values, not continuity of the discrete optimal-memory threshold.
hypotheses: Fixed finite Hilbert dimension and fixed finite command and reset-report alphabets.
Valid primitive reset data with positive mean cost floor and no closed failure set.
A fixed finite live memory M with the pure-start observation and counting conventions of thm:r78-reset-frontier.
statements.identity: R78 numbered author addition; the inventory includes lemmas and corollaries and is not a novelty or editorial verdict.
internal_load_bearing_facts: The full-support one-label reset transition matrix is transient, so its resolvent and cost cap are locally continuous.
An attaining deterministic-report controller is transient from every reset state; its fixed rows and selector remain proper under sufficiently small perturbations.

Locally bounded minimizing supersolutions have convergent subsequences with a fixed selector. A finite limit supersolution is a valid controller certificate even if it exceeds a particular chosen limiting cap.
statements.label: prop:r78-frontier-stability
statements.limits: Dimensions and alphabets are fixed; perturbations remain valid reset instruments with a positive cost floor and no closed failure set. The discrete threshold can jump, including when failure effects vanish.
statements.proof: Upper semicontinuity follows by retaining an attaining controller: its transient reset matrix has spectral radius below one, and the continuation resolvent and spectral start cost vary continuously. A full-support proper row provides locally uniform upper bounds. For lower semicontinuity take attaining certificate sequences, extract convergent rows and bounded continuation vectors with a constant selector, and pass the closed supersolution and spectral inequalities to the limit. The resulting finite supersolution constructs a proper controller. The unrestricted value is a fixed sufficiently-large-memory value, so strict gaps persist.

statements.claim_class: A closed all-memory cost spectrum and exact synthesis formula for every finite action-cover incidence system in the retained physical reset family, not merely its saturation threshold.
classical_ingredients: Finite Bellman equations with action-independent transition
Capped simplex linear optimization and rearrangement
Finite lower envelopes of affine functions
statements.conclusion: The exact entire frontier is V_M=3+r/(1-r)+min_(H:|H|<=M-1) min_(1<=k<=q) [1+lambda sum_(j<=k) b_(j)(H)]/k. An optimum uses pure continuing rows and an initial row uniform on k smallest uncovered-penalty actions. The finite enumeration includes arbitrary ties and r=0. After the common term is subtracted, each fixed-M frontier is a continuous nondecreasing piecewise affine concave function of lambda.
hypotheses: The explicit reset family associated with nonempty proper subsets A_1,...,A_s of [q], q>=2: reset states e_i, E_(a,i)=(r/s)I, cost entries 1+1_(a notin A_i) on e_i and 3+1_(a=j) on f_j.
0<=r<1, finite live memory M>=1, and the same all-initial-state pure-start controller class.
H is a set of at most M-1 continuing pure actions; U(H) are the uncovered A_i, b_a(H) counts uncovered sets omitting a, and lambda=r/[s(1-r)].
statements.identity: R78 numbered author addition; the inventory includes lemmas and corollaries and is not a novelty or editorial verdict.
internal_load_bearing_facts: For fixed rows, reset transition probabilities are action-independent. The Bellman value is x_i=1+h_i+r(1+mean h)/(1-r), h_i=min_k p^k(A_i^c).
The f_j eigenvalues of the initial cost operator strictly dominate all e_i eigenvalues.
At a global row-list optimum, each continuing row can be replaced in succession by a vertex because its separate objective is concave; the initial row is not subjected to this false purification.

The remaining min_p(max p+lambda b dot p) has a minimizer uniform on a subset, by a capped-simplex exchange argument and piecewise-affine endpoint reduction. Existence is claimed; ties may permit additional nonuniform optima.
statements.label: thm:r78-cover-frontier
statements.limits: The set-system enumeration retains combinatorial hardness; there is no claim of a polynomial algorithm. Pure continuation is proved for this family, not for arbitrary reset instruments. The original quantum discrimination risk and timing frontiers remain different problems.
statements.proof: Solve the row-choice Bellman equations explicitly for action-independent reset transitions, compute the dominating start eigenvalues, and obtain the compact continuous row objective. Separate concavity allows all rows except the initializer to be purified at an optimum. They form H; hit states have zero penalty and unhit states have the initializer penalty, producing b(H) dot p. Introducing t>=max p reduces the linear allocation to saturating the smallest coefficients; on each interval [1/(k+1),1/k] the result is affine, so t=1/k endpoints and uniform supported rows suffice. Finite minimization proves the formula and realization. The endpoint r=0 and positive-r cover threshold are checked separately.

statements.claim_class: An explicit arbitrary-length exact memory hierarchy with matched optimal upper and lower values, a strict comparison with the inherited one-residual lower certificate, and persistence beyond commuting primitive effects.
classical_ingredients: Spectral norm perturbation bounds for largest eigenvalues
statements.conclusion: For the unperturbed rational instrument V_M=4+1/n+(n-1)max(n-M+1,0)/n^2, giving n consecutive strict gaps with success probability 1/2 and actual costs in [1,4]. Its first-residual certificate is exactly D_M=(V_M-V_*)/2. The strict hierarchy persists in a valid open neighborhood and under the explicit noncommuting effect perturbation. The latter has positive failure/success effects, unchanged mean cost operators I<=G_a<=4I, a joint physical paid-cost realization with costs {1,9}, and |V_M(epsilon)-V_M(0)|<=4epsilon.
hypotheses: For every n>=2 take the explicit action-cover instrument with s=q=n, A_i={i}, r=1/2, in Hilbert dimension 2n.
M>=1 live labels with counted pure initialization, mandatory success stopping and no additional observations.
For the noncommuting perturbation, X=|e_1><f_1|+|f_1><e_1| and only E_(1,1) is changed by epsilon X, with 0<epsilon<(n-1)/(8n^2).
statements.identity: R78 numbered author addition; the inventory includes lemmas and corollaries and is not a novelty or editorial verdict.
internal_load_bearing_facts: For u uncovered singleton sets, b_a=u-1 on uncovered actions and u on covered actions. The minimizing initializer can be uniform on all n actions; maximizing H gives u=max(n-M+1,0).
The first-residual certificate replaces lambda=1/n by 1/(2n); its separately solved minimum is exactly half the full excess cost in this family only.

The offdiagonal perturbation has zero expectation at every reset state, leaving all palette continuation problems unchanged with x_i<=4. The initial operator changes by epsilon p^1_1 x_1 X, of norm at most 4epsilon.

The noncommuting cost/report assignment is physically realizable: charge one on failures and split success into F_9=(G-I)/8 and F_1=B-F_9, charged nine and one. Both effects are positive for the specified epsilon, sum to B, and yield mean cost G without exposing cost as a new report.
statements.label: cor:r78-strict-hierarchy
statements.limits: n>=2 is necessary for strict gaps. The exact formula and D_M ratio concern only the unperturbed displayed family. Perturbed mean costs retain [I,4I], but the demonstrated physical realized cost support is {1,9}, not [1,4]; initial success probability need not remain exactly 1/2. No other paper frontier or general quantum advantage is inferred.
statements.proof: Evaluate the finite cover-spectrum formula by the two ranges k<=u and k>=u, showing a minimum at k=n and then largest allowable H. Repeat with the first-residual coefficient to compute D_M. Continuity protects the finite collection of gaps. For explicit noncommuting perturbations verify positivity of E and B, a nonzero commutator with G_1, unchanged reset expectations, and the uniform 4epsilon spectral perturbation bound. Adjacent gaps stay larger than (n-1)/n^2-8epsilon. A success-effect split supplies a full CP joint report/cost realization, avoiding any unproved compatibility of noncommuting cost and failure observables.
